                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the structural characteristics of pathogenic viruses. Cell cultures infected by different viruses are observed under a scanning electron microscope. One of the cell samples is infected by a virus that has an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules. The most likely virus that has infected this cell sample can cause which of the following conditions?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Yellow fever
opb. Shingles
opc. Erythema infectiosum
opd. Ebola
ope. Condylomata acuminata
"

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The virus with an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules suggests it may replicate in the nucleus and utilize host cellular machinery. Among the options, the Ebola virus is known to have an envelope and causes hemorrhagic fever, aligning with the characteristics of enveloped viruses. The Varicella-Zoster Virus (Shingles) also has an envelope but is not derived from nuclear membrane molecules. Erythema infectiosum is caused by Parvovirus B19, which does not have an envelope from nuclear membranes, making it less likely. Yellow fever virus is an enveloped RNA virus but does not specifically relate to nuclear membrane characteristics. Condylomata acuminata is caused by HPV, which lacks an envelope from nuclear membranes. Therefore, the most likely virus that has infected the cell sample is the Ebola virus, which can cause hemorrhagic fever.
